key_insight: The paper couples differentiable manufacturing constraints with inverse-homogenization optimization and a progressive Pareto-front learning strategy to efficiently generate manufacturable lattice designs.
engineering_relevance: This helps additive manufacturing engineers design lattice metamaterials that better balance performance and printability, while exploring multiple objectives under limited optimization budgets.
method: Embed differentiable constraints for overhangs, enclosed cavities, and powder-removal channels directly into topology optimization.
Use a density-generation network to learn latent representations of high-quality lattices and initialize new optimizations from interpolated nondominated samples.
Iteratively update the network with newly found nondominated solutions to expand the manufacturable Pareto set.
evidence_signal: On 3D periodic unit cells across 1000 optimization runs, network initialization improved success rate to 92.60% and produced 916 manufacturable samples versus 78.30% and 776 for random initialization, with hypervolume increasing from 0.0675 to 0.0787.
watch_item: The approach depends on learned initializations and constraint formulations, so performance may vary with lattice class, material system, and the fidelity of manufacturing constraints used in practice.
paper_title: Lattice Structure Optimization for Additive Manufacturing: Manufacturability-Driven Design and Pareto Front Construction
